NoteNlpAccessor::remove_hashtags¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteNlpAccessor::remove_hashtags() const

Delete Hashtag Tokens Without Damaging Embedded Hashes¶

remove_hashtags() removes social-style hashtag tokens while preserving the surrounding sentence and its punctuation. It is the deletion counterpart to mask_hashtags(): choose removal when the tag itself contributes no useful signal, and masking when the downstream consumer should retain the fact that a tag occupied that position.

A recognized token has two parts:

Part

Rule

Left boundary

Start of the cell, or one byte that is not an ASCII letter, digit, or underscore

Hashtag

# followed by one or more ASCII letters, digits, or underscores

The left-boundary rule is important. #release_2, (#team), and [#ops] match, but the hash in mid#word does not begin a token because it follows an ASCII letter. C# and a bare # also remain because there is no tag body after the hash. The operation is deliberately ASCII-lexical: it does not infer language-specific word boundaries or extend a tag through punctuation.

Only the hash and its tag body are deleted. Boundary punctuation remains, so (#team) becomes () and [#ops] becomes []. If at least one token is removed, remaining ASCII whitespace is collapsed and stripped. If no token matches, the cell is returned byte-for-byte, preserving newlines and edge spaces rather than normalizing unrelated text.

The result is a fresh Text Note with the receiver’s rank and shape. Cells are processed independently; a hashtag-only cell becomes "", not an absent cell. Undefined Notes propagate, empty Notes preserve their shape, and Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes are rejected before any cell is transformed. A cheap # precheck avoids regular-expression work for cells that cannot match.

Example 1: Tokens At Whitespace And Punctuation Boundaries¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({
        "Ship #release_2 with (#team), [#ops]; keep C# mid#word and #"})
        .nlp().remove_hashtags()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Ship with (), []; keep C# mid#word and #"]

The punctuation is evidence that this operation removes the token rather than the entire punctuation-delimited region around it.

Example 2: Embedded And Empty Hash Forms Are Exact No-Ops¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"  C#\nmid#word stays  "})
        .nlp().remove_hashtags()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["  C#\nmid#word stays  "]

No recognized tag was removed, so the leading spaces, newline, and trailing spaces survive exactly.

Example 3: Removal Is Cell-Wise And Shape-Preserving¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a@b.io", "Page 1", "#tag", "<b>bold</b>"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix.nlp().remove_hashtags()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a@b.io", "Page 1"], 
  ["", "<b>bold</b>"]
]

The email, footer-like text, and markup belong to other removal families and are not changed merely because they share the same Note.
